newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN says aid work for east Zaire refugees resumed.
newsitem.headline: UN says aid work for east Zaire refugees resumed.

text.p: Western relief agencies in east Zaire resumed aid work for 160,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees on Friday after negotiating an end to a brief suspension ordered by local authorities, the United Nations refugee agency UNHCR said.

But at the same time, UNHCR said local officials barred foreign relief planes from landing directly at the regional hub of Kisangani, a centre for distribution of aid and also the main base for Zaire's army fighting Tutsi-led rebels in the region.
Spokeswoman Pamela O'Toole said UNHCR was informed by the governor of Haut Zaire region that aid planes would be allowed in Kisangani only if they came through Zaire's capital Kinshasa.
"This would be very time-consuming and costly," she said.

In Lubutu, 240 km (150 miles) southeast of Kisangani, where UNHCR earlier reported a suspension of relief work ordered by officials, O'Toole said aid agencies resumed activities after negotiations with a local governor.
O'Toole said delivering aid to the refugees was increasingly risky because of worsening security and fighting in the region.

UNHCR had no details of the fighting, but reports from the region on Thursday said Tutsi-led rebels, fighting a Zairean counter-offensive, were advancing towards Lubutu -- a key town on the road to Kisangani, the Zairean army's main base.
Some 120,000 Hutus are camped out in Tingi-Tingi, a tiny Zairean village some seven km (four miles) east of Lubutu, and another 40,000 in Amisi, 70 km (44 miles) to the southeast.
The refugees in Lubutu trekked deeper west into Zaire after Tutsi rebels overran their camps in October rather than join 600,000 who returned home to Rwanda.

The UNHCR says they are accompanied by soldiers of Rwanda's former Hutu government army which played a key role in 1994's Hutu-led genocide of Tutsis, after which the Hutus fled to east Zaire in fear of retribution.
